transcript:
Header: 2027-05-12 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52 mins | Location: Zoom
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Patel (Redwood SE), Sarah Kim (MountainView Head of IT), Dr. Miguel Torres (Clinical AI Lead), Priya Shah (Security Architect), Liam O'Rourke (PM)

Summary: quick intro, then deep dive into security/compliance checklist for the pilot, data handling, SSO, RBAC and audit requirements. Benchmarks and workload sizing discussed; agreed on next steps.

00:00 Speaker 1 (Ava): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm ava chen, i'm the AE on this, with diego our solutions eng. you all good to go?
00:10 Speaker 2 (Sarah): yep thanks ava. i'm sarah kim, head of it at mountainview. joining from boston. we have priya on security and miguel on clinical ai, liam will chime on timelines.
00:22 Speaker 3 (Diego): hi folks, short agenda: security/compliance items, workload sizing and perf expectations, success criteria for the POC, and logistics — sso, audit logs, kms. does that cover it?
00:30 Speaker 4 (Priya): yes, our focus is the security posture. we can do standard pilot if we see the right controls — SOC 2 + ISO attestation, SSO, RBAC, and enriched audit logs. we also need data residency assurances.
00:44 Speaker 1 (Ava): totally. quick framing: our usual pilot is 4 weeks, hosted or private. for security-first customers we offer Private (VPC) deployments or Dedicated with strict tenancy and KMS integration. for the pilot we typically run either a Hosted-with-contract + SOC2 attestation or a short Dedicated sandbox. which do you prefer?
00:59 Speaker 2 (Sarah): prefer private or dedicated sandbox. since PHI/lightweight clinical notes might be in scope, we need KMS/HSM integration and SOC2. is redwood SOC 2 type II?
01:10 Speaker 1 (Ava): yes we have SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 attestation, i'll share the reports. for KMS we support customer-managed keys for private deployments and bring-your-own-KMS for Dedicated.
01:22 Speaker 3 (Priya): we also need SSO — SAML 2.0 — so our admins can manage access. RBAC granularity matters: ability to restrict model deployment, see logs but not download raw transcripts, and separate roles for engineering vs clinical reviewers.
01:36 Speaker 2 (Diego): RBAC we support role mappings and can integrate with your IdP. we also have token-level auditing and per-route permissions. small caveat — some of the hosted features like automated autoscaling baked into the multi-tenant control plane have different audit retention policies; for the pilot we can set a 90-day retention or push to your archive.
01:58 Speaker 4 (Miguel): on the workload side — typical load for the pilot will be about 5000 requests/day, peak concurrency about 20 requests at once, avg tokens per request ~300, p95 lat target <350ms for short generations but we understand clinical prompts vary. want a benchmark run with our anonymized sample.
02:20 Speaker 3 (Diego): good data point. for sizing we'd run a bench with 1k concurrent sessions and scale down; but given your numbers we can propose a 2-GPU Dedicated sandbox (NVIDIA A100 class) with batching and prefix cache tuned; that should easily meet p95 <400ms and cost predictable. we'll validate with the bench.
02:42 Speaker 1 (Ava): success criteria — what do you want to see to call the pilot successful?
02:48 Speaker 4 (Priya): for security: SOC2 attestation provided, SSO setup, RBAC mapping for at least 3 roles, ability to forward audit logs to our SIEM (Splunk), KMS with customer-managed keys. for functionality: latency p95 within target on our sample, throughput as measured, and acceptable redaction/masking support for PHI.
03:12 Speaker 5 (Liam): timeline wise we want to go live with the pilot by June 7 and complete in 4 weeks, assuming legal and security review happen quickly. procurement's touchpoints will be minimal if we get the attestation and contract terms.
03:26 Speaker 2 (Diego): noted. on audit logs — we can stream rich logs with request id, user id, model version, token counts, and optional redact/omit fields. does mountainview need logs in a specific schema or to push to Splunk?
03:41 Speaker 4 (Priya): push to Splunk preferred, prefer syslog/HTTPS collector. retention policy 1 year for the pilot artifacts, and encryption at rest/in transit is mandatory.
03:54 Speaker 3 (Diego): we support push to HTTPS endpoint and S3 archive. for privacy we can mask tokens and redact detected PHI. caveat: automatic redaction is probabilistic; we recommended you run an eval to check coverage.
04:15 Speaker 1 (Ava): on legal side, we'll send our standard pilot MSA and a security questionnaire response pack. can you flag any non-standard requirements?
04:24 Speaker 4 (Priya): we have a handful: data residency (US-only), no outbound copy of raw transcripts outside the VPC, and need an SLA for availability during the pilot window.
04:35 Speaker 2 (Diego): we can do US-only region for Private/Dedicated. for hosted, we can limit region routing but not full tenancy isolation. SLA — we can provide a pilot-level availability target; production SLA discussions are separate.
04:52 Speaker 4 (Priya): thank you. also need to validate model governance — ability to pin model versions and see changelogs. we want deterministic rollbacks in case of regression.
05:03 Speaker 3 (Diego): rollouts + pinning are supported; we'll show the console in the follow-up demo.
05:12 Speaker 1 (Ava): ok let's talk benchmarks — what does mountainview want measured?
05:18 Speaker 4 (Miguel): latency p50/p95, token throughput per GPU, and semantic quality baseline (ROUGE-like or custom eval) on a 200-sample prompt set. also cost per 1k tokens estimate.
05:30 Speaker 2 (Diego): we'll do perf runs with your 200 anonymized prompts at different concurrency points: 1, 5, 20 concurrent, measuring p50/p95/p99 and GPU util. we'll provide a spreadsheet with results. any special instrumenting required?
05:45 Speaker 4 (Priya): please include GPU memory footprint and quantization profile if you test quantized variants. we may prefer 8-bit quantized for cost.
05:56 Speaker 3 (Diego): noted — we'll include quantized runs.
06:02 Speaker 1 (Ava): data handling — priya, do you need on-prem connector or is VPC enough?
06:08 Speaker 4 (Priya): VPC is fine if logs and keys stay in our control. no egress of raw transcripts. KMS with customer-managed keys is mandatory.
06:18 Speaker 2 (Diego): our private mode supports BYOK and HSM-backed KMS on supported clouds; for pilot we'll document exact key rotation and guardrails.
06:27 Speaker 4 (Priya): also, we need RBAC mapping to our IdP groups: devs, clinicians, auditors. clinicians should have query and read-only access to outputs, devs can deploy/test, auditors can only view logs.
06:43 Speaker 3 (Diego): we map IdP groups to our roles; can enforce per-route permissions. we'll share a sample mapping file for your IdP.
06:52 Speaker 1 (Ava): any regulatory flags — do you have HIPAA BAA requirement?
06:56 Speaker 4 (Priya): yes, we need HIPAA BAA for any PHI processing. is that possible during pilot?
07:04 Speaker 1 (Ava): Redwood can sign BAAs in private/dedicated deployments; for hosted pilots we often use contractual guardrails until BAA is in place. we'll get legal to confirm and include in the packet.
07:16 Speaker 5 (Liam): on timeline — immediate blockers are security review and legal. once we get SOC2 + BAA confirmation and the sample data, we can schedule bench the week of May 24.
07:28 Speaker 2 (Diego): ok we'll prepare a test harness and perf scripts. can you provide a sample of typical prompts — styles and token lengths?
07:36 Speaker 4 (Priya): yes i'll share a zipped sample anonymized set and a mapping for expected redaction fields (mrn, names, dob) by 2027-05-18.
07:46 Speaker 1 (Ava): great. i'll attach the SOC2 report, ISO cert, and a one-pager on our private deployment options. we'll also include an architecture note about audit log streaming.
07:56 Speaker 3 (Miguel): question on quality monitoring — do you have regression alerting tied to prompt sets? we need to know if model changes affect outputs mid-pilot.
08:05 Speaker 2 (Diego): yes we have Evaluate/Monitor tooling — you can bind prompt sets and get alerts on quality regressions; for the pilot we'll lock model versions but still run continuous evals.
08:18 Speaker 4 (Priya): excellent. final set of security checks we will do: verify SOC2 + ISO docs, perform a light pen test or scan, validate SSO+RBAC, check audit streaming to Splunk, verify KMS configuration and docs, and run bench.
08:36 Speaker 1 (Ava): sounds good, i'll summarize next steps in an email and share docs. any other concerns?
08:42 Speaker 4 (Priya): one more — data retention policy on transcripts: we want an option to auto-delete after 30 days or archive into our S3 with server-side encryption.
08:53 Speaker 2 (Diego): we can set retention rules and automatic archiving to your S3 with SSE-KMS. we'll document the artifact lifecycle.
09:02 Speaker 5 (Liam): ok, recap timeline: docs out by 5/14, sample data by 5/18, bench w/c 5/24, pilot start on 6/7. deliverables: security packet, bench plan, POC scope and pricing.
09:22 Speaker 1 (Ava): perfect, thanks everyone. we'll follow up in email and schedule the bench kickoff.
09:30 Speaker 2 (Sarah): thanks, talk soon.

END TRANSCRIPT

Notes: minor transcription artifacts: "K-V cash" typed once instead of KV cache, a few names slightly garbled (Migel vs Miguel) in auto transcript.
